name: Hakone-Yumoto
description: The main entry point where the Romancecar and Hakone Tozan railway meet, Hakone-Yumoto is the town's busiest hub. A riverside street of shops, snack stalls, cafes, and long-established onsen ryokan makes it the most convenient and lively base for a first stay.
bestFor: First-timers and travelers wanting easy transport and amenities
pros: Easy onward transport into the Hakone loop
cons: Less scenic than the higher villages

name: Gora
tagline: Hillside hot springs and art museums
description: Perched up the Hakone Tozan railway line, Gora is a quieter hillside village known for quality ryokan, private onsen, and nearby art museums including the famous open-air sculpture park. It sits at the junction of the cablecar, making it a scenic and well-connected mid-mountain base.
bestFor: Slow-travel nomads wanting quiet, art, and good onsen

name: Sengokuhara
tagline: Highland plateau of grass and calm
description: A spacious highland area famous for its silver pampas grass fields that glow in autumn, Sengokuhara is the most open and tranquil part of Hakone. Spread out and served mainly by bus, it offers boutique ryokan, small museums, and a slower, more rural pace among the mountains.
bestFor: Deep-rest seekers and nature lovers wanting space
pros: Wide open scenery and pampas grass fields

name: Moto-Hakone
tagline: Lakeside shrine and the iconic torii
description: On the southern shore of Lake Ashi, Moto-Hakone is home to the Hakone Shrine and its celebrated red torii gate rising from the water. A sightseeing-boat stop with lakeside inns and cafes, it delivers the classic postcard views of the torii and, on clear days, Mount Fuji.
bestFor: Photographers and those chasing the iconic lake views
pros: Best Mount Fuji lake views on clear days
Sightseeing boat access across Lake Ashi
cons: Farther from rail, bus and boat dependent
